elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: §21.1 as rendered: "each Party's total aggregate liability ... shall not exceed the greater of ..." and "The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims." Pre-existing favourable language retained unchanged.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Rendered §21.1: "the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement and all Order Forms, including subscription fees, in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000." Basis is "fees paid or payable" (not broader "all amounts"), lookback anchored to the claim, and lowercase "fees" plus the express reference to all Order Forms and subscription fees defeats the illusory §1.5 defined "Fees" (USD 12,000 Implementation Fee under the first Order Form only).

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: §21.2 untouched: "neither Party is liable for indirect, incidental, special, exemplary, punitive, or consequential damages, or for lost profits, revenues, or goodwill" — bilateral by its terms.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: §21.3 Excluded Claims (carved out of the §21.1 cap by "Except for Excluded Claims") includes "a Party's breach of confidentiality ... obligations".

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: §21.3: "breach of confidentiality, data-protection, or security obligations" sits within Excluded Claims, outside the cap.
§21.3: "its indemnification obligations" is an Excluded Claim, so indemnities sit outside the mutual cap.
§21.3: "gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud" listed as Excluded Claims.
§21.3: "gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud" listed as Excluded Claims.
§21.3: "... or fraud" included in Excluded Claims, excepted from §21.1 and §21.2.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: §21.3: "infringement or misappropriation of the other Party's intellectual property" is an Excluded Claim; mutual direction preserved.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: §21.3 retained: "Customer's obligation to pay undisputed Fees for conforming Services is not damages and is not limited by this Section." Existing language left untouched.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: §21.1: "each Party's total aggregate liability ... The cap is mutual."

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: §21.1 as rendered measures the cap by "the fees paid or payable by Customer ... in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim" (with a USD 1,000,000 floor), no longer confined to the USD 12,000 Implementation Fee under the first Order Form.
§21.3 Excluded Claims include "its indemnification obligations"; §21.1 opens "Except for Excluded Claims".

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: §21.3 Excluded Claims include "a Party's breach of confidentiality ... obligations".

reasons: Deviation call is correct: the pre-edit cap was measured by defined "Fees" (§1.5–1.6 = a one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee) and further confined to the first Order Form, i.e. an illusory cap far below six months' fees — walk-away territory under LOL-CAP.
All eleven preferred elements are met on the rendered operative language; the position is complete at the preferred level (and a fortiori at the fallback).

The cap element is repaired in substance, not merely mechanically: the drafter used lowercase "fees" and expressly reached "this Agreement and all Order Forms, including subscription fees", so the narrow §1.5 definition and the "first Order Form" restriction cannot be re-imported. The basis is "paid or payable" (not the broader "all amounts") and the lookback runs from the claim, matching the element literally.

Minimal: only the measuring language in the first sentence of §21.1 was changed. The mutuality sentence, §21.2 mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages (including the Customer-favourable direct-damages sentence), and the whole of §21.3 Excluded Claims and the payment-obligations carve-out are retained verbatim. No survival tail, expense language, extra damages categories, procedures or boilerplate were added, and the words added beyond the bare formula are necessary to defeat the illusory defined term.

Preserves intent: §1.5–1.6 are left intact so every other reference to "Fees" (payment, invoicing, §21.3's "undisputed Fees") still resolves; no dangling cross-reference, undefined term, or retained sentence contradicts the new cap. The USD 1,000,000 floor and the mutual structure are internally consistent with "Except for Excluded Claims" in §21.1 and §21.2.

Non-blocking notes for the drafter: (i) the temporal anchor was shortened from "the event giving rise to the claim" to "the claim" — this matches the element text exactly but is a marginally narrower trigger than the model language, so consider restoring "the event giving rise to the claim" if the counterparty resists; (ii) §21.3's payment carve-out still references defined "Fees" (USD 12,000), which is Customer-favourable and correctly left alone under this rule; (iii) the narrow §1.5 "Fees" definition may need attention under the fees/payment rule, not here.
